concept: Steel & Steam: Cafe Madras, Matunga East (1940). A kinetic word-stack opens on the cafe name; four different dishes, four different motions (dosa crack, idli dunk and tear, vada press with ripples, sheera scoop), rack focus between plate and steam, no pours; the steel tumbler language (steel plates, katori bowls) ties the scenes together; ends on the large Bombay Cafe Map lockup held 3 s.

alternatives.note: recommended: kinetic stack + rack focus on steel thali props

dimensions.palette: banana-leaf green #14312A (ground), steel #B5BDC2, jasmine white #F4F6F1, kolam cobalt #4F7DF0 (accent). No orange, no cream, no pink, no red. Not the palettes of Slow Cafe, Mondegar, Kyani or Acquisition Lore.
dimensions.fonts: Bricolage Grotesque variable (width and weight swing) + DM Mono labels, two faces only
dimensions.opening: cafe name first: kinetic stack, 'CAFE' and 'MADRAS' slam in and resize to fill the frame width over the illustrated dosa (L051)
dimensions.transition: steel-plate wipe: a brushed-steel disc scales from the hero dish to cover the frame, then reveals the next scene
dimensions.camera: rack focus between plate and steam, slow push-ins on flat 2D plates; map dive with a real-node pin
dimensions.layout: centred stacked title, place-card tags bottom-left, dish names set in white on green
motion_device: real-node pin drop with sonar pulse
dimensions.texture: flat editorial illustration with fine paper grain on a brushed-steel table; 3D map only for the city
dimensions.sound: stack thuds, crisp dosa crack, steam, spoon on steel, soft pad; voice at most 1.5 words per second; no pouring
dimensions.ending: green end card, large real Bombay Cafe Map stacked lockup with @bombaycafemap and bombaycafemap.com, 'Cafe Madras, Matunga East, since 1940' as the second large line, held 3 s

experiment.hypothesis: A name that fills the frame in the first second holds attention better than a small stamped title
